stem: During the Pandavas' year in disguise at King Virata's court (Mahabharata, Virata Parva), what role did Arjuna take?
options: a cook and wrestler called Vallava
a dice-playing courtier called Kanka
a eunuch dance teacher, Brihannala
a keeper of the horses, Granthika
why: Arjuna lived as the eunuch Brihannala, teaching song and dance to princess Uttara; Vallava was Bhima, Kanka was Yudhishthira and Granthika was Nakula (Mahabharata, Virata Parva 2).

es.stem: durante el año en que los Pandavas vivieron disfrazados en la corte del rey Virata (Mahabharata, Virata Parva), ¿qué papel asumió Arjuna?
options: un cocinero y luchador llamado Vallava
un cortesano jugador de dados, Kanka
un eunuco maestro de danza, Brihannala
un cuidador de caballos, Granthika
es.why: Arjuna vivió como el eunuco Brihannala, maestro de canto y danza de la princesa Uttara; Vallava era Bhima, Kanka era Yudhishthira y Granthika era Nakula (Mahabharata, Virata Parva 2).

stem: In the Mahabharata's episode of the Yaksha's questions, why does Yudhishthira ask that Nakula be revived rather than Bhima or Arjuna?
options: so that Madri, like Kunti, would still have a living son
because Nakula was the youngest and most helpless brother
because Nakula had not drunk from the yaksha's lake
because the yaksha had offered to revive the weakest one
why: Yudhishthira, Kunti's son, chooses Madri's son Nakula so that both of Pandu's wives keep a living son; pleased, the yaksha, revealed as Dharma, revives all four (Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Yaksha-prashna).

es.stem: en el episodio de las preguntas del yaksha en el Mahabharata, ¿por qué Yudhishthira pide que reviva Nakula y no Bhima ni Arjuna?
options: para que Madri, como Kunti, tuviera todavía un hijo vivo
porque Nakula era el hermano más joven y más indefenso
porque Nakula no había bebido del lago del yaksha
porque el yaksha había ofrecido revivir al más débil
es.why: Yudhishthira, hijo de Kunti, elige a Nakula, hijo de Madri, para que las dos esposas de Pandu conserven un hijo vivo; complacido, el yaksha, que resulta ser Dharma, revive a los cuatro (Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Yaksha-prashna).

stem: In the Drona Parva, why does Karna's use of Indra's Shakti dart against Ghatotkacha matter so much for Arjuna?
options: the dart passed to Ashvatthama, who later turned it on Arjuna
it was a weapon made for rakshasas, with no power over men
using it broke Karna's oath and kept him off the field a day
it could be thrown once, so it was spent before he met Arjuna
why: Indra's dart, given in exchange for Karna's armor and earrings, could kill one foe and then return to Indra; spent on Ghatotkacha, it could no longer kill Arjuna, as Krishna explains (Mahabharata, Drona Parva, Ghatotkacha-vadha).

es.stem: en el Drona Parva, ¿por qué importa tanto para Arjuna que Karna use contra Ghatotkacha el dardo Shakti de Indra?
options: el dardo pasó a Ashvatthama, que luego lo lanzó contra Arjuna
era un arma hecha para rakshasas, sin poder contra los hombres
usarlo rompió el juramento de Karna y lo alejó un día del campo
se podía lanzar una vez, así que se gastó antes de enfrentar a Arjuna
es.why: El dardo de Indra, dado a cambio de la armadura y los aretes de Karna, podía matar a un solo enemigo y luego volvía a Indra; gastado en Ghatotkacha, ya no podía matar a Arjuna, como explica Krishna (Mahabharata, Drona Parva, Ghatotkacha-vadha).

stem: In the Karna Parva, Krishna tells of the ascetic Kaushika, who truthfully showed robbers where travelers were hiding. Applying that teaching to a new case, how should a villager who truthfully tells a mob where a hunted innocent is hiding be judged?
options: as right, since a true statement carries no fault in itself
as wrong, since truth is weighed by its effect on living beings
as blameless, since the guilt falls on the mob that acts on it
as right, provided the villager had taken a solemn vow of truth
why: Krishna says Kaushika suffered for his truthful answer, because what is true is judged by the good it does to beings, not by the letter of a vow (Mahabharata, Karna Parva, Krishna's counsel to Arjuna).
source: Mahabharata, Karna Parva (the stories of Kaushika and Balaka)

es.stem: en el Karna Parva, Krishna cuenta la historia del asceta Kaushika, que con verdad les mostró a unos ladrones dónde se escondían unos viajeros. Aplicando esa enseñanza a un caso nuevo, ¿cómo se juzga a un aldeano que con verdad le dice a una turba dónde se esconde un inocente perseguido?
options: como correcto, porque una afirmación verdadera no tiene falta en sí
como incorrecto, porque la verdad se mide por su efecto en los seres
como libre de culpa, porque la culpa es de la turba que actúa
como correcto, si el aldeano había hecho un voto solemne de verdad
es.why: Krishna dice que Kaushika sufrió por su respuesta verdadera, porque lo verdadero se juzga por el bien que hace a los seres, no por la letra de un voto (Mahabharata, Karna Parva, consejo de Krishna a Arjuna).

stem: In the Stri Parva of the Mahabharata, what does Gandhari's curse on Krishna foretell?
options: that his brother Balarama would one day turn on him in battle
that he would lose his sight, as she had given up her own
that his own clan, the Vrishnis, would destroy one another
that his name would be forgotten in the land of the Kurus
why: Blaming Krishna for not preventing the war, Gandhari curses that his kinsmen, the Vrishnis, will slay one another in the thirty-sixth year, which comes true in the Mausala Parva (Mahabharata, Stri Parva 25).

es.stem: en el Stri Parva del Mahabharata, ¿qué anuncia la maldición de Gandhari contra Krishna?
options: que su hermano Balarama un día se volvería contra él en batalla
que perdería la vista, como ella había renunciado a la suya
que su propio clan, los Vrishnis, se destruiría a sí mismo
que su nombre sería olvidado en la tierra de los Kurus
es.why: Culpando a Krishna por no impedir la guerra, Gandhari lo maldice: sus parientes, los Vrishnis, se matarán entre sí en el año treinta y seis, lo que se cumple en el Mausala Parva (Mahabharata, Stri Parva 25).

stem: In the Ashvamedhika Parva, what does the half-golden mongoose claim about Yudhishthira's horse sacrifice?
options: it is worth less than a poor family's gift of flour to a guest
it is void, since the horse was seized from a defeated king
it is flawed, since Krishna stayed away from the whole rite
it cannot wash away the sin of Drona's death by a lie
why: The mongoose turned half golden by touching the flour left from a gleaning brahmana family's gift of their last barley to a hungry guest, who was Dharma in disguise, and says the great rite does not equal it (Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva).
source: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva (the mongoose and the gleaning brahmana)

es.stem: en el Ashvamedhika Parva, ¿qué afirma la mangosta medio dorada sobre el sacrificio del caballo de Yudhishthira?
options: vale menos que la harina que una familia pobre dio a un huésped
es nulo, porque el caballo fue tomado de un rey vencido
tiene un defecto, porque Krishna no asistió a todo el rito
no puede lavar el pecado de la muerte de Drona por una mentira
es.why: La mangosta quedó medio dorada al tocar la harina que sobró cuando una familia pobre de brahmanes espigadores dio su última cebada a un huésped hambriento, que era Dharma disfrazado, y dice que el gran rito no se le iguala (Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva).

stem: In the Stri Parva, Vidura consoles the grieving Dhritarashtra with the parable of a man hanging in a well. In one or two sentences, what does the parable teach about human life?
why: Vidura explains the forest as samsara, the well as the body, the serpent as Time, the rats as days and nights and the honey as pleasures: people keep craving sweetness while time consumes them (Mahabharata, Stri Parva 5–6).
source: Mahabharata, Stri Parva 5–6 (Vidura's parable of the man in the well)

rubric.point: says life is hemmed in by death or time that is steadily running out (the serpent, the elephant, or the rats gnawing as days and nights)
says the man still reaches for the drops of honey: people keep craving small pleasures in spite of the danger
decodes at least one other figure correctly (well = body, forest = samsara, serpent = Time, elephant = the year)
links it to Vidura's counsel that grief cannot undo what time brings, so one should turn to detachment and dharma

es.stem: en el Stri Parva, Vidura consuela al afligido Dhritarashtra con la parábola de un hombre colgado en un pozo. En una o dos oraciones, ¿qué enseña la parábola sobre la vida humana?
es.why: Vidura explica que el bosque es el samsara, el pozo es el cuerpo, la serpiente es el Tiempo, las ratas son los días y las noches y la miel son los placeres: la gente sigue deseando lo dulce mientras el tiempo la consume (Mahabharata, Stri Parva 5–6).

stem: At the end of the Mahaprasthanika Parva, why does Yudhishthira refuse to enter heaven in Indra's chariot without the dog, and who does the dog turn out to be?
why: Yudhishthira says that forsaking one who is devoted to him is as grave a sin as killing a brahmana; the dog then reveals itself as Dharma, his father, who praises his compassion (Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva 3).

rubric.point: says he will not abandon a devoted companion who depends on him, since forsaking the devoted is a grave sin in his eyes
identifies the dog as the god Dharma (Yama-Dharma), Yudhishthira's father, who was testing him
notes that Dharma had tested him before, as the yaksha at the lake

es.stem: al final del Mahaprasthanika Parva, ¿por qué Yudhishthira se niega a entrar al cielo en el carro de Indra sin el perro, y quién resulta ser el perro?
es.why: Yudhishthira dice que abandonar a quien le es fiel es un pecado tan grave como matar a un brahmán; entonces el perro se revela como Dharma, su padre, que alaba su compasión (Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva 3).
